source.title: AllClear: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Cloud Removal in Satellite Imagery
source.authors: Hangyu Zhou; Chia-Hsiang Kao; Cheng Perng Phoo; Utkarsh Mall; Bharath Hariharan; Kavita Bala

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own training-data scaling results for satellite-image cloud removal and downstream segmentation, extending the scaling question to an image-based task. It does not test language-model cross-entropy scaling.
record.gate_note: The data-size sweeps and the downstream segmentation comparison are the study's own results. Other benchmark comparisons and temporal-length or modality ablations do not bear on the listed scaling versions and are not included.
record.test_reason: This is a satellite cloud-removal dataset paper. It sweeps UnCRtainTS training-data size (1%, 3.4%, 10%, 100%; about 2.8k to 279k samples, single run each, no error bars) and calls the gains a "scaling law", but it fits no power law and reports no loss curve. Four unreplicated points of PSNR, SSIM, SAM and MAE cannot show whether the power-law form of V5 holds. Read off the table, the points are irregular: PSNR rises about 4.5 dB from 3.4% to 10%, then 0.9 dB from 10% to 100%; SAM is non-monotonic in Table 4. The downstream segmentation comparison has only two data sizes, and segmentation is done by a separate UNet fed cloud-removal outputs, so it shows no predictable scaling relation (V6). The data-size finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that prior cloud-removal models are undertrained and that AllClear's larger training set significantly improves performance. They say the "scaling law" holds under both Sentinel-1 preprocessing methods, and that AllClear-trained models help downstream segmentation. They use "scaling law" to mean that more data helps; they fit no power law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a satellite-image cloud-removal data-size sweep using UnCRtainTS and image reconstruction metrics, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling or a fitted power-law recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Sentinel-1 gap-filling preprocessing changes the reported scaling results; the study reports separate sweeps with the original and zero-filled setup.

fits_no_version.finding: In satellite cloud removal (UnCRtainTS), training on more data generally improves reconstruction metrics from 1% to 100% (PSNR 27.0 to 33.9 in Table 4; 32.0 to 34.1 with zero-filled Sentinel-1 gaps in Table 7). Gains are irregular and some metrics are non-monotonic. The shape of the curve depends on how Sentinel-1 gaps are filled.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-reconstruction quality of cloud-removal models improves with training-set size, without an established functional form.

fits_no_version.finding: Land-use segmentation on cloud-removal outputs is slightly better with the 100% AllClear model than the 10% model (Jaccard 0.604 vs 0.591).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More cloud-removal training data transfers to small downstream segmentation gains.

record.peer_reviewed: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024), Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
record.problems: No error bars are reported, and the checklist says they did not report error bars. The study reports discrete training-data-size comparisons rather than fitted power-law curves; it does not report total compute or hardware in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Non-scaling ablations and baseline benchmark comparisons were not included.

untested.parts: All: no fitted law and no extrapolation.
All: no compute or model-size variation.
Power-law form in image models: data size is varied, but no fit is made and four single-seed points cannot establish the form.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss: only two data sizes are compared.

missing.what: Training on full AllClear improves accuracy for low and medium cloud cover but not for fully clouded regions (100% AllClear vs SEN12MS-CR-TS). This is a condition where more data does not help.
Table 12 gives 100% AllClear uncorrupted PSNR 33.352 and SAM 5.618, inconsistent with Table 4 (33.868, 5.232).

record.verdict_notes: Not a language-model scaling study. The 1% row in Table 4 shares SSIM, SAM and MAE exactly with the pretrained SEN12MS-CR-TS model in Table 2, suggesting a possible table error. No seeds, error bars or compute are reported. The reader's V6 'supports' label was removed: two data sizes evaluated through a separate segmentation model do not test predictable downstream scaling.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation for language models.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
The study varies training-data size for image cloud-removal models, but does not fit or verify a power-law form; it does not test the other listed modalities or regimes.
The study reports downstream segmentation results for two cloud-removal training-data sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship or test language-model downstream tasks or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and departures from power laws.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AllClear-trained cloud-removal models used for land-use segmentation, comparing 10% with 100% training data
reader_labels.reason: All five reported downstream metrics improve for the 100% model relative to the 10% model (rows T11-Jaccard-10, T11-Jaccard-100, T11-F1-10, T11-F1-100, T11-Accuracy-10, T11-Accuracy-100, T11-Precision-10, T11-Precision-100, T11-Recall-10, T11-Recall-100).
